findings.description: The whole S2-MOM-v1 experiment is outside version control: src/stage3/, scripts/run_s2_mom*.py, scripts/build_stage3.py, seven test files, the delivery cost schedules, addendum 1 and supplements 1-4, the deviation log, data/stage3/, results/s2_mom_v1*/, the manuscript, and 21 registry + 6 trial lines are untracked or uncommitted. The registry's freeze_commit and environment.git_commit (7d4cb6d) contain none of this code.
findings.why_it_matters: There is exactly one copy of the registered code and results, on one disk. git clean -fd, git stash -u, a bad checkout or a disk fault destroys it. No third party can obtain the code that produced the registered hashes. 'git_dirty: true' is the only trace.
findings.reproduction: git status --short | grep '^??' ; git ls-files src/stage3 (empty) ; git show 7d4cb6d --stat (protocol only)
findings.expected_behavior: Registered code, inputs manifests, results and registry lines are committed; the registry names a commit that contains them.
findings.actual_behavior: 112 changed/untracked paths; registered experiment code not in any commit.
findings.proposed_fix: Commit the current tree as it is (no content change, so every SHA-256 stays the same); tag it; record the commit id in a registry amendment. Decide whether data/india collector changes go in the same or a separate commit.
findings.regression_test: Test: every path in the registered CODE tuples, every registered result file and the Stage 3 manifest is tracked by git (git ls-files --error-unmatch) and unmodified at HEAD.
findings.evidence: VERIFIED BY INSPECTION (git status, git ls-files)
findings.remediation: CLOSED 2026-10-08. Research release committed (f5bfed89bc7b1bd258dbe81ff9da2be8f44acbdc), tagged s2-mom-v1-release-1, pushed to the private origin; data archive packed to an external USB drive and verified; a fresh clone of the tag with the data restored from that drive passed the suite and the reproduction (F01_CLOSURE_PLAN.md, Closure record). Before that: all research-critical files staged for one commit. Large data outside Git: content-addressed archive manifest (5,637 files, SHA-256 each), deterministic tar hash, manifest and tar hash anchored in the registry, verify/pack/materialize tool. Guard test fails on any untracked or merely ignored research file.
findings.adversarial_test: tests/test_release_archive.py: changed, missing, extra file; rewritten manifest; wrong tar; path traversal; symlink; no overwrite
findings.evidence_after: F01_CLOSURE_PLAN.md Closure record: remote ref and tag verified, USB tar SHA-256 bb4b9659...1ac2 re-read, fresh clone 960 passed (tag) / 964 passed (main), reproduction PASS in a clean Conda environment.

findings.description: data/stage3/s2_mom_v1/manifest.json is the only integrity anchor for the Stage 3 inputs (calendar, universes, identity, sessions, gap rows, panel). The manifest itself is anchored nowhere: its hash is not in the registry (provenance.data_manifest is a path), not in code, and the file is untracked. verify_provenance() checks Stage 2 inputs and three code files, not the Stage 3 outputs.
findings.why_it_matters: Inputs and manifest can change together (hand edit, or delete-and-rebuild after any upstream change) and the runner accepts them. The hash chain from registry to the numbers the ladder reads has a missing link.
findings.reproduction: On a scratch copy: append one byte to primary/calendar.csv -> load_inputs raises. Put the new hash into manifest.json -> load_inputs returns normally.
findings.expected_behavior: A changed Stage 3 input is refused even if the manifest was changed with it.
findings.actual_behavior: Accepted silently once the manifest matches.
findings.proposed_fix: (a) Record the SHA-256 of the manifest 'content' block in the registry by an amendment (value today is consistent with the registered results: proven by the audit recomputation). (b) Add a verification command and a test that compare the manifest with the registered value. Enforcing it inside the runner would change scripts/run_s2_mom.py (frozen) - do that only in a later protocol version.
findings.regression_test: Test: tampered Stage 3 file + rewritten manifest is rejected by the verifier; registered manifest hash equals the file on disk.
findings.remediation: Registry anchor (line 59) of the Stage 3 manifest SHA-256; verifier walks registry -> manifest -> files, Stage 2 inputs, code hashes; exact file set; no symlink, traversal or duplicate entry.
findings.adversarial_test: tests/test_provenance_chain.py; tests/test_failure_injection.py: 18 file attacks on inputs, manifest, code
findings.evidence_after: PROVENANCE_VERIFICATION_REPORT.md; mutation group 'guards and registry' (provenance mutations)

findings.description: The registry is not a state machine. amend() accepts any field: status FINAL -> PLANNED, a new protocol_sha256, a provenance block that replaces (not merges) the registered run hashes, an empty reason. current() lets a second line with the same experiment_id discard every earlier amendment. No file lock, no fsync, no checksum chain; appends are plain open('a'). A truncated last line makes the whole registry unreadable (fail loud, no recovery tool).
findings.why_it_matters: The registry is the root of trust for 'what was registered'. Any helper, test or hand edit can re-point a registered result to different hashes or flip its status without an error.
findings.reproduction: On a scratch copy: experiments.amend('S2-MOM-v1','x',status='PLANNED'); amend(..., protocol_sha256='0'*64); amend(..., provenance={'primary_run': {...}}); amend(..., ''); append a duplicate record line -> current()['S2-MOM-v1']['status'] == 'PLANNED'.
findings.expected_behavior: Invalid transitions, changes to protected fields, loss of registered hashes, empty reasons and duplicate ids are refused.
findings.actual_behavior: All accepted. Only an unknown id or an unknown status string is refused.
findings.proposed_fix: In experiments.py (not part of any registered code hash): protected-field list (experiment_id, protocol_sha256, freeze_commit, universe_sha256, registered files_sha256 of an existing run); allowed status transitions; non-empty reason; current() raises on a duplicate id; append under an exclusive lock with flush+fsync; each new line carries the SHA-256 of the previous line. Must accept the existing 58 lines unchanged.
findings.regression_test: State-machine tests: FINAL -> PLANNED refused; protected field change refused; registered run hashes cannot be dropped or altered; duplicate id raises; existing registry file still folds to the same current() view (golden).
findings.remediation: src/registry/experiments.py rewritten: state machine, protected fields, explicit revalidation, full amendment metadata, hash chain, pinned history, fail-closed reader, lock + fsync.
findings.adversarial_test: tests/test_registry_state_machine.py: 156 state pairs, forged amendments with a valid chain, parser attacks, history rewrites; tests/test_failure_injection.py: 11 registry attacks on a copy of the real registry
findings.evidence_after: REGISTRY_SECURITY_REPORT.md; the 58 historical lines fold to the pre-remediation view (hash pinned in a test)

findings.description: 24 of 104 deliberate mutations of critical logic pass the whole 451-test suite. Among them: WML = W + L; step D drops the exit-session return; step D uses raw returns on every row; the H1 decision threshold reversed; a one-sided bootstrap count; the Stage 3, RET-1.1 and UNIV-1 hash checks switched off; the run-once guard switched off; confirmation allowed without a same-code primary run; cost rates taken at the exit date; identity links from the future; liquidity window 64 instead of 63. src/stage3/data.py has 26 % line coverage; scripts/run_s2_mom.py 52 %; src/registry/experiments.py 54 %.
findings.why_it_matters: These are exactly the 'dangerous bug that keeps every test green' cases. The registered numbers are right today (proven by independent recomputation) but the suite would not notice if the code were changed tomorrow.
findings.reproduction: See MUTATION_TEST_REPORT.md; each survivor was applied to a scratch copy and the full suite run. Three were re-confirmed by hand (451 passed).
findings.expected_behavior: Every listed mutation fails at least one behavioural test.
findings.proposed_fix: Add tests only (no source change): see TEST_GAP_MATRIX.md G-01..G-16.
findings.regression_test: Re-run the mutation set; target: zero survivors in the 'research logic' and 'guards' groups.
findings.evidence: PROVEN BY TEST (mutation run on scratch copies)
findings.remediation: Tests written against the surviving mutations: hand-computed golden ladder world, hand Newey-West, both bootstrap tails, 12-row decision table, runner gates, loader hash checks, Stage 2 rules, step E rates; mutation campaign tool with recorded batches.
findings.evidence_after: MUTATION_FINAL_REPORT.md

findings.description: There is no executable reproduction or verification of the registered results. The 'golden' tests only hash the result files. Registered modes refuse to rerun by design, and no verify mode recomputes and compares. A clean clone also lacks the inputs: data/raw/nse_archive, data/stage2/datasets and panel.parquet are git-ignored, and the NSE list snapshots cannot be re-downloaded in their original version.
findings.why_it_matters: The stated standard is independent verifiability. Today it needs the original laptop plus new code written by the verifier.
findings.reproduction: grep -n 'hashed only' tests/ ; .gitignore ; scripts/run_s2_mom.py _write
findings.expected_behavior: A documented command recomputes the A-D series, delta, H1 and step E from the Stage 3 inputs with independent code and compares with the registered files at a stated tolerance.
findings.actual_behavior: No such command. The audit wrote one outside the repository (all 680 step-months and all step E months match to <= 5e-16).
findings.proposed_fix: Add scripts/verify_s2_mom.py (the audit's independent implementation), an opt-in slow test that runs it when the git-ignored inputs are present, and a deposit plan for the git-ignored inputs (archive with checksums).
findings.regression_test: pytest -m golden: independent recomputation equals registered monthly/delta/step E files within 1e-9.
findings.evidence: VERIFIED BY INSPECTION; recomputation PROVEN by the audit script
findings.remediation: scripts/reproduce_s2_mom_v1.py: 8 steps, independent implementation of ladder A-D, delta, Newey-West, step E costs, C2 arithmetic; read-only; fail closed.
findings.adversarial_test: tests/test_failure_injection.py: 46 file attacks through the verification steps
findings.evidence_after: REPRODUCTION_REPORT.md: PASS in the registered interpreter and in a clean Conda environment; 8,257 numbers, all within 1e-9; largest difference 6.7e-14

findings.description: No dependency is pinned and there is no lock file. numpy, scipy and pyarrow are used by the experiment and not declared. The registry environment block of the primary, sensitivity, confirmation and step E runs records neither scipy (p-values) nor pyarrow (parquet bytes behind the input hashes). The lab runs in the shared base Anaconda environment.
findings.why_it_matters: The exact environment of the registered runs cannot be rebuilt from the repository, and a routine conda update changes it silently.
findings.reproduction: cat requirements.txt ; python3 -c "from src.registry.experiments import environment; print(environment())"
findings.expected_behavior: Exact versions of every package on the research path are pinned in the repository and recorded with each run.
findings.actual_behavior: Eight unpinned names; scipy/pyarrow unrecorded for four of five runs.
findings.proposed_fix: Add pinned requirement files (versions in DEPENDENCY_AUDIT.md); add scipy, pyarrow and platform to environment(); record the environment observed on 2026-10-07 by a registry amendment labelled 'observed after the fact'; use a project virtual environment.
findings.regression_test: Test: environment() contains every package imported under src/stage2, src/stage3, src/registry; pinned file equals installed versions.
findings.remediation: Conda contract (environment.yml, conda-osx-arm64.lock), ENVIRONMENT.json and requirements-lock.txt (exact pins), anchored in the registry (lines 60 and 61); environment() records scipy, pyarrow, platform; verifier reports versions, missing, mismatched and unloadable libraries.
findings.adversarial_test: tests/test_failure_injection.py: 3 environment-metadata attacks; tests/test_environment.py: simulated missing / mismatched / unloadable library
findings.evidence_after: DEPENDENCY_FINAL_REPORT.md: official environment = Conda osx-arm64; clean Conda rebuild reproduces (PASS); pip unsupported and documented; second machine untested (N-01).

findings.description: The matrix builder does not validate the values it is given. Duplicate (date, entity) rows: the last one wins. A return of -100 % becomes -inf, below -100 % becomes NaN, +inf stays inf. A research-grade row with a missing return becomes 0. An unknown class value is treated as 'no information' (return 0, not flagged). mean_test returns NaN for NaN input without raising, and the section 27 decision then reads INCONCLUSIVE.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the UNTRUSTED -> TRUSTED boundary for the numbers the ladder uses. Today it is safe only because the input file is hash-pinned and happens to be clean.
findings.reproduction: Audit attack script, section 'ladder numerical / structural inputs' (all seven cases accepted silently).
findings.expected_behavior: Fail loudly on duplicates, non-finite or <= -1 returns, a missing return on a research-grade row, an unknown class, and NaN in a test series.
findings.actual_behavior: Accepted silently. The registered panel has none of these (checked: 2,115,961 rows).
findings.proposed_fix: Report only. A validation function could live outside the frozen files (called by the verifier of F-05); a guard inside wide()/mean_test belongs to the next protocol version.
findings.regression_test: Property tests: each malformed input raises.
findings.evidence: PROVEN (attack script); registered data verified clean by the audit
findings.remediation: Frozen ladder.wide() unchanged. Outside it: integrity.validate_stage3 rejects duplicates, NaN, inf, returns <= -100%, unknown classes, wrong counts, before any recomputation; the comparison refuses NaN/inf.
findings.evidence_after: FAILURE_INJECTION_REPORT.md section 4.2. The frozen runner path itself still does not validate; it cannot run again for v1.

findings.description: Output writing is neither atomic nor exclusive. _write checks exists() and then calls write_text (race between two processes; a kill mid-write leaves a partial JSON that then counts as 'already exists'). The five CSV files are written with plain to_csv after the JSON. The trial log and the registry amendment come last. The run-once check happens after the whole analysis has been computed.
findings.why_it_matters: A crash between the first write and registration leaves a complete, readable primary or confirmation result that is unregistered and absent from the trial log. The natural recovery (delete and rerun) is an unrecorded second look.
findings.reproduction: Read lines 96-107: _write(json) -> to_csv x5 -> log_trial -> _amend.
findings.expected_behavior: Check run-once before computing; write everything into a temporary directory, fsync, rename once; log the trial start before computing and the completion after.
findings.proposed_fix: Report only (frozen file). Until then: operational rule in the runbook - never delete a result file; record any crashed run in the deviation log and the trial log by hand.
findings.regression_test: Kill-during-write test on a temporary directory: no final file, rerun allowed only after an explicit recorded reset.
findings.remediation: Frozen runner unchanged (documented limitation). Registered outputs cannot be replaced silently: hash check, unregistered-file check, registry refuses re-registration on FINAL. New tooling writes tmp + fsync + rename.
findings.adversarial_test: tests/test_failure_injection.py: truncate an output, add an unexpected file (results), unregistered rerun
findings.evidence_after: REMEDIATION_REPORT.md section 8

findings.description: The code hashes do not cover everything the runs execute. Main: not src/intraday/inference.py (bootstrap), src/stage2/returns.py (JUMP), src/access.py, src/config.py, src/registry/experiments.py. Step E: only step_e.py and its runner - not stats.py (the Newey-West test) and protocol.py (alpha, lags, slippage table), which it imports. C2: only the script - not stats.py. Library versions are in no hash.
findings.why_it_matters: 'Same code hash' is weaker than it reads: a change in an imported module would not invalidate a protected run.
findings.reproduction: Compare each CODE tuple with the import graph.
findings.expected_behavior: The hash covers the transitive first-party imports of the runner.
findings.actual_behavior: Partial lists. Mitigation today: inference.py is pinned by the ORB frozen-hash test; stats.py and protocol.py are in the main hash, which still equals the registered value.
findings.proposed_fix: Report only (frozen files). Add a test, outside the frozen files, that pins the SHA-256 of every first-party module imported by each runner.
findings.regression_test: Test: import-graph of each runner is a subset of the pinned file list.
findings.evidence: VERIFIED BY INSPECTION; SUPPORTED BY HASH for today's state
findings.remediation: Registered code hashes cannot be widened without changing registered values. Every executed first-party file, hashed or not, is now pinned to the pre-remediation snapshot by a test.
findings.adversarial_test: mutation campaign: resampler and Stage 2 mutations killed behaviourally
findings.evidence_after: A library upgrade is still outside every hash; the numerical comparison of the reproduction is the control.

findings.description: Safeguards are written as assert statements: the seven structural checks of the Stage 3 build (last session = T*, 170 months, 114/56 split, step A/B/C universe sizes and identities), the cutoff consistency checks, and the ORB evaluator's session-window check. python -O or PYTHONOPTIMIZE removes them.
findings.why_it_matters: A safeguard that an environment variable can switch off without a message is not fail-closed.
findings.reproduction: python3 -O -c "print(__debug__)" -> False; the checks are 'assert' lines.
findings.expected_behavior: Checks raise an explicit exception in every interpreter mode.
findings.proposed_fix: Report only for the frozen files. Low-cost mitigation outside them: the verifier (F-05) repeats the structural checks with explicit raises; the runbook forbids -O.
findings.regression_test: Run the verifier under python -O in a test.
findings.remediation: 13 assert statements inventoried (7 data.py, 1 protocol.py, 1 access.py, 4 evaluate_orb_v1.py). The 9 on the S2-MOM path are restated as explicit raises (validate_stage3, validate_cutoffs). The reproduction refuses python -O.
findings.adversarial_test: tests/test_failure_injection.py: last session is not T*, 113 months, 199-stock universe, step A list changes
findings.evidence_after: The 4 asserts of the ORB evaluator are not restated (single-use frozen evaluator; runbook rule).

findings.description: The environment variable TRADING_LAB_NO_TRIAL_LOG (meant for tests) silently disables trial logging for any real run started from a shell where it is set. The runners do not check the return value.
findings.why_it_matters: The trial count is the basis of the multiple-testing statements. A silent zero is worse than an error.
findings.reproduction: TRADING_LAB_NO_TRIAL_LOG=1 python3 -c "from src.registry import experiments as E; print(E.log_trial('k',{},'d',{},'s'))" -> None
findings.expected_behavior: A real run cannot proceed without a trial record; only the test harness can suppress it.
findings.actual_behavior: Returns None; run continues and registers.
findings.proposed_fix: In experiments.py: suppress only when pytest is running (PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST present) or via an explicit function argument; otherwise raise if the variable is set.
findings.regression_test: Test: with the variable set and no pytest marker, log_trial raises.
findings.remediation: log_trial: the variable suppresses logging only inside pytest; anywhere else it raises.
findings.adversarial_test: mutation '+ trial log silenced outside pytest'
findings.evidence_after: REGISTRY_SECURITY_REPORT.md

findings.description: Two gates rest on hand-editable evidence. The pre-run check gate reads a local JSON file (all_passed, code_sha256) that carries no registered hash; 'checks' mode may be rerun at will. The Stage 2 gate tests only that the registry field stage2_rebuild.checks_passed equals 150; that field was written by a manual amendment, not by build_stage2.py.
findings.why_it_matters: The gates prove that a file or a number exists, not that the check ran.
findings.reproduction: Read lines 59-62 and 78-79; registry line 40 (amendment of 2026-10-05T20:51:33).
findings.expected_behavior: The script that performs the check writes the evidence and its hash to the registry itself.
findings.actual_behavior: Manual registration; unanchored check files. The manuscript builder also reads these two files.
findings.proposed_fix: Report only for the runner (frozen). Now: record the SHA-256 of the two pre_run_checks files in a registry amendment; add them to the verifier.
findings.regression_test: Test: check files equal their registered hashes.
findings.remediation: Pre-run check files and the Stage 2 rebuild log anchored in the registry; the reproduction requires all_passed with the registered code hash and recounts 150 OK lines in the log.
findings.evidence_after: PROVENANCE_VERIFICATION_REPORT.md section 4 (residual: the log proves no change since 2026-10-07, not what happened on 2026-10-05)

findings.description: GET /api/add downloads a Yahoo history and overwrites data/india/<symbol>d1.csv in place, non-atomically, with no confirmation. The symbol is used in the file name after removing only '.NS', '.BO', '^', '&' (path separators and '..' are not rejected). State-changing GET; no authentication. fetch_data.py overwrites data files the same way.
findings.why_it_matters: Research data files that registered legacy experiments identify by SHA-256 can be replaced from a browser tab. README note 1 documents that this already happened once (a figure became irreproducible after a refresh).
findings.reproduction: Read lines 83-102.
findings.expected_behavior: POST only; strict symbol pattern; refuse to overwrite an existing file (write a new dated file instead); atomic write.
findings.proposed_fix: Fix in server.py (not frozen): validate with a regular expression, use POST, refuse existing targets.
findings.regression_test: Tests: '../x', 'a/b' rejected with 400; an existing file is not overwritten.

findings.evidence_after: THREAT_MODEL.md T13

findings.description: The launchd collector appends to 58 git-tracked data files in the research working tree every weekday, so the tree is permanently dirty and the registry's git_dirty flag is always true. The last run (2026-10-06 19:03) exited 1: BELm15.csv and CIPLAm15.csv were rejected because one overlapping bar disagreed by more than 0.2 %.
findings.why_it_matters: git_dirty cannot distinguish 'collector ran' from 'code was edited'. Rejected holdout bars are lost for good if not recovered inside Yahoo's 60-day window (ORB v1 holdout completeness).
findings.reproduction: tail logs/collector.log ; data/raw/collection_log.jsonl run 20261006T190331
findings.expected_behavior: Collector output is separated from the code tree or committed by its own job; rejections raise an alert.
findings.actual_behavior: Dirty tree; exit code 1 visible only in a log file.
findings.proposed_fix: Operational: review the two rejections; commit collector data separately; make environment() report code dirtiness and data dirtiness separately.
findings.regression_test: holdout_status already reports health; add the last collector exit code to it.
findings.remediation: Not changed. The snapshot verifier and the reproduction now separate collector files from research files. The collector exited 1 again on 2026-10-07 18:30.
findings.evidence_after: logs/; needs the researcher's review inside Yahoo's 60-day window

findings.description: Any HTTP 200 response body is stored as a permanent raw file and recorded with its hash. There is no check that the body is a zip (bhavcopy) or JSON (corporate actions), no size check, no fsync. Raw files are never overwritten, so a truncated or HTML error body stays until someone edits the archive and the manifest by hand.
findings.why_it_matters: A partial download poisons the append-only archive. It is detected later (the parser raises on a bad zip), so it is loud, but recovery is manual surgery on an 'append-only' record.
findings.reproduction: Read lines 76-91.
findings.expected_behavior: Validate the payload before recording status 200; otherwise treat as a transient failure.
findings.proposed_fix: Changing archive.py changes a hash embedded in the Stage 2 manifests (code_sha256), so treat as frozen: report only. Mitigation: the Stage 2 rebuild opens every file.
findings.regression_test: Test with a fake opener returning HTML: nothing recorded.
findings.remediation: No change (archive.py hash is embedded in Stage 2 manifests). Every archived raw file is now also in the external archive manifest.

findings.description: A portfolio-month with no ledger row gets cost 0 through fillna(0.0), and the guard only requires costed months to be a subset of gross months. The module's own header says no cost is ever set to zero.
findings.why_it_matters: If holdings for one portfolio-month were missing or dropped, its net return would silently equal its gross return.
findings.reproduction: Read lines 280-284.
findings.expected_behavior: Raise when a (portfolio, month) has no cost row.
findings.actual_behavior: Filled with 0. Not triggered: every one of the 170 months has a positive cost for W, L and the benchmark (verified).
findings.proposed_fix: Report only (frozen file). The verifier asserts 'every month has a positive cost'.
findings.regression_test: Test: remove one month from the ledger -> error.
findings.evidence: VERIFIED BY INSPECTION; non-occurrence PROVEN by the audit script
findings.remediation: Frozen step_e.net_returns unchanged. Outside it: validate_step_e and a registered-file test reject any zero, missing or non-finite cost; the independent cost function raises on a missing rank.
findings.evidence_after: every registered month has a positive cost (340 months x 15 columns)

findings.description: The single-use ORB v1 holdout evaluator has 26 % line coverage; its body is exercised only by two manual dry runs on development data (identical results). Outputs are written file by file and registered afterwards; a crash in between consumes the single use without a registry record (fail closed, but unrecoverable without a manual decision).
findings.why_it_matters: It can run only once on the real holdout. A defect found on the day cannot be fixed without breaking the frozen hashes.
findings.reproduction: coverage report; read lines 244-292.
findings.expected_behavior: An end-to-end test of the evaluator on synthetic sessions, including the refusal and crash paths.
findings.actual_behavior: Not tested end to end by the suite.
findings.proposed_fix: Add tests only (no change to the frozen evaluator or its frozen modules).
findings.regression_test: Synthetic end-to-end test in a temporary repository.
findings.remediation: Not changed (ORB v1 evaluator, not S2-MOM).
findings.evidence_after: forensic TEST_COVERAGE_AUDIT.md

findings.description: The 'gap return already booked' set is kept per portfolio. A gap return booked by W in month m could be earned again by L in month m+1 if the stock moved between them. Occurrences in the registered runs: 0 (checked for every step, both samples).
findings.why_it_matters: Possible double counting across portfolios of the same step.
findings.reproduction: Audit script counter 'cross-portfolio re-count': 0.
findings.expected_behavior: A booked row is consumed for every portfolio of the step, or the rule is documented.
findings.proposed_fix: Report only (frozen). Note for the next protocol version.
findings.regression_test: Synthetic test of a stock moving W -> L across a suspension.
findings.remediation: No change. The independent implementation applies the same per-portfolio rule; cross-portfolio re-count in the registered runs: 0 (forensic audit).
findings.evidence_after: note for S2-MOM-v2

findings.description: Duplicated rules and constants: the 'unadjustable event' pattern exists in returns.py and again in ladder.py; three union-find implementations with two entity-id conventions; Holm in inference.py and in the C2 runner; one-sided Newey-West test in step_e.py and the C2 runner; the same SHA-256 constants are typed into protocol.py, both later runners, build_stage2.py, the manuscript builder, several tests and the documents; two cost models (costs.py and step_e.py).
findings.why_it_matters: A rule changed in one place only gives inconsistent results that no hash detects.
findings.reproduction: grep.
findings.expected_behavior: One authoritative implementation or constant, imported everywhere.
findings.proposed_fix: Tests that assert the copies are equal (pattern strings, hash constants versus registry). No frozen file needs to change.
findings.regression_test: Equality tests.

findings.description: Protocol section 14 defines the Sharpe-type ratio of long-only portfolios as the information ratio against the step's benchmark. The code reports mean/sd for every portfolio. The metric is not in the DEV-2 list of unexecuted analyses.

findings.reproduction: Read _describe.

findings.proposed_fix: Add to the deviation log (researcher's decision).

findings.description: Decision order: a significant estimate whose 90 % interval lies wholly inside +/-0.10 is labelled DETECTED_SIZE_UNCERTAIN; the protocol table can also be read as 'immaterial'. The rule is also evaluated for the confirmation sample (already disclosed in the registry). The flipped-threshold mutation survives the suite.
findings.why_it_matters: Label ambiguity; untested labelling code.
findings.reproduction: Read lines 271-273.
findings.expected_behavior: A reviewer ruling and a table-driven test of all four labels.
findings.actual_behavior: Not triggered: the primary result is INCONCLUSIVE.
findings.proposed_fix: Add tests of the four labels (no source change); record the ruling.
findings.regression_test: Four-label test.
findings.remediation: No change to the rule. All four labels are now pinned by a 12-row table test and by a check that the registered labels follow from the registered numbers.

findings.evidence_after: the reading 'significant but inside +/-0.10 = DETECTED_SIZE_UNCERTAIN' still needs a reviewer ruling

findings.description: The Newey-West lag is looked up by sample name, not computed from the number of months actually tested. If months were unpaired the lag would not follow the frozen formula. Both registered samples are fully paired (114, 56), where the constants equal the formula.
findings.why_it_matters: Silent drift from the formula in an edge case.
findings.expected_behavior: Lag computed from n, or a guard that n equals the nominal sample size.
findings.proposed_fix: Report only (frozen).
findings.regression_test: Assert n == nominal in the verifier.
findings.evidence: VERIFIED BY INSPECTION; PROVEN equal for registered runs
findings.remediation: No change. Guard from outside: tests and the reproduction check that the lag equals floor(4 (n/100)^(2/9)) for the registered n.
findings.adversarial_test: mutations 'NW lag primary 4->5', '+ NW lag OOS 3->4'

findings.description: Numeric fields are coerced (malformed -> NaN) and rows whose date cannot be parsed are dropped from the date comparison, then stamped with the file's session date. Both are counted in QA only as missing prices.

findings.remediation: No change (Stage 2 code hash embedded in manifests).

findings.description: Delisting class is decided by a case-sensitive substring test for 'Voluntary' in free text copied from the NSE file. Current values are exactly 'Voluntary Delisting', 'Compulsory Delisting', 'Delisting - Liquidation' (checked).

findings.proposed_fix: Report only (frozen).

findings.evidence: VERIFIED BY INSPECTION; values PROVEN on registered data
findings.remediation: No change. Guard from outside: validate_delisting_types fails on any delisting wording other than the three known ones.
findings.evidence_after: observed: Voluntary Delisting, Compulsory Delisting, Delisting - Liquidation

findings.description: The placebo gate requires p > 0.05 for one fixed seed, so it fails for about 5 % of seeds by construction. Confirmation-sample value: p = 0.054.

findings.reproduction: data/stage3/s2_mom_v1/checks/pre_run_checks_oos.json
findings.expected_behavior: A rule for what happens on failure, fixed in advance.
findings.proposed_fix: Disclosure only.
findings.evidence: SUPPORTED BY the saved check file
findings.remediation: No change. Disclosure item: the placebo gate has a built-in 5% false-failure rate (p = 0.054 in the confirmation sample). The check files are now anchored.

findings.description: Reproduction is defined as byte identity of CSV and parquet files. That holds on this machine and library set; another numpy/pandas/pyarrow version or CPU can change the last digit or the parquet encoding, and the rebuild is then refused although the numbers agree.
findings.why_it_matters: Fail-closed is right for protection, but it makes cross-machine verification fail for reasons unrelated to the science.
findings.expected_behavior: A second, tolerance-based comparison for verification purposes.
findings.proposed_fix: Provide the tolerance-based verifier of F-05; keep byte identity for the protected runs.
findings.regression_test: Golden test at 1e-9.
findings.remediation: The reproduction compares numbers at 1e-9 and reports environment differences; frozen byte-identity checks are unchanged for the protected runs.
findings.adversarial_test: mutations '+ repro: tolerance 1e-9 -> 1', '+ repro: comparison never fails'
findings.evidence_after: REPRODUCTION_REPORT.md

findings.description: Any Python session can import the Stage 3 modules and compute any sample's results directly. load_inputs calls only verify_protocol(); there is no decision gate, no primary-before-confirmation order, no run-once guard and no trial log on this path.
findings.why_it_matters: The protection of the confirmation sample 'comes from the execution order and the code hash' (protocol B3); the execution order is enforced only inside one script.
findings.reproduction: By inspection of the function signatures; a notebook (Untitled.ipynb) lives in the repository root.
findings.expected_behavior: The data loader refuses unless called through the registered runner, or logs a trial itself.
findings.proposed_fix: Report only (frozen). Runbook rule; the verifier (F-05) is the one sanctioned read path and logs its own use.
findings.remediation: Frozen modules can still be imported and called directly. A result computed that way cannot be registered on the FINAL experiment; an extra trial-log line fails the reproduction. A private computation that logs nothing cannot be prevented by code.
findings.evidence_after: THREAT_MODEL.md T4; runbook rule 3

findings.description: Reproducibility contract. Found during remediation: a fresh venv built with pip from the pinned versions cannot load scipy 1.15.3 on macOS 27 arm64 (the PyPI wheel has a malformed zero-fill section that the loader rejects); the reproduction fails closed. Resolved: the official environment is stated as Conda osx-arm64 (environment.yml, conda-osx-arm64.lock), pip is documented as unsupported, and a clean Conda environment built from environment.yml reproduced the results (PASS). Still open: no second machine, OS or CPU has been tried, and the lab's daily work still runs in the shared Anaconda base environment.
findings.why_it_matters: Third-party reproduction is demonstrated on one machine only. A conda update of the base environment changes the study's environment.
findings.proposed_fix: Run the reproduction once on a second Apple-silicon Mac; work in the dedicated s2mom environment.
findings.evidence: DEPENDENCY_FINAL_REPORT.md; REPRODUCTION_REPORT.md runs C, D, E

findings.description: Table A5 printed the hashes of the protocol, Addendum 1 and Supplements 1 and 4, but not of Supplements 2 and 3. Fixed 2026-10-08: both added to the builder's hash list (each recomputed and matched at build time); manuscript rebuilt, presentation only.

findings.description: Removing lines from the END of the registry leaves a valid shorter history. It is detected only where something depends on those lines (the reproduction requires the anchors and state FINAL) and by Git.
findings.why_it_matters: Tail truncation is not caught by the registry module alone.
findings.proposed_fix: Push the repository; optionally pin the registry head hash in each release note.

findings.description: The six sensitivity treatments and the reverse-order ladder are not recomputed by the independent implementation; they are verified by hash, by code hash and by internal arithmetic only. The bootstrap p-value is recomputed with the registered resampler, not a second one.
findings.why_it_matters: For these numbers the evidence is 'unchanged since registration', not 'independently reproduced'.
findings.proposed_fix: Extend the independent implementation, if the researcher wants that evidence.

findings.description: The laptop holding the only copy has about 3 GB of free disk and several GB of swap in use. During remediation a parallel test run filled the disk once (on scratch clones only; the repository was verified intact afterwards).
findings.why_it_matters: A full disk can interrupt a write of the registry or of the collector, and it blocks making the archive tar.
findings.proposed_fix: Free disk space (about 2 GB of stale scratch copies from the forensic audit session are under /private/tmp/claude-501/); then pack the archive to external storage.
